questions.q: Which work area is where you enter, apply and reverse customer payments?
questions.explain: The Receipts work area covers entering receipts, applying them to transactions, automatic receipts, lockbox, and reversals.

questions.q: What does a transaction's completion status (Incomplete/Complete) describe?
options: Whether the transaction is finished being entered and eligible for accounting
Whether the transaction has been printed
questions.explain: Completion status is about whether entry is finished. Balance status (Open/Closed) is the separate concept that tracks payment.

questions.q: Can a transaction be Complete and still Open at the same time?
options: No, Complete always means fully paid
No, completion and balance status are the same field
Yes — Complete means entry is finished; Open means the balance is still due, and both can be true for a long time
Only credit memos can be Complete and Open simultaneously
questions.explain: Completion status and balance status are independent. A complete invoice sits Open until it's paid, credited, or written off.

questions.q: What triggers the accounting (debit/credit) entries for a Receivables transaction?
options: The Create Accounting process, which runs once the transaction is Complete
questions.explain: A transaction must be Complete before Create Accounting can derive its journal entry and, depending on options, post it to General Ledger.

questions.q: Which work area holds the Receivables setup tasks like transaction types, sources, and activities?
options: The Setup and Maintenance work area, under the Receivables functional area
They are configured directly in General Ledger
questions.explain: Setup tasks live in Setup and Maintenance, separate from the day-to-day Billing, Receipts, Customers and Collections work areas.
